newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes mixed but improves on budget.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes mixed but improves on budget.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed mixed on Thursday, but recovered from early weakness as the government's presentation of its 1997 budget eased speculation, traders said.
"The peso was under pressure and jitters abounded all day, until the budget guidelines were released to Congress. That set dealers minds at ease and the peso recovered," said a trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 0.9 of a centavo firmer at 7.9160/7.9230 per dollar, while its 24-hour stablemate closed 0.8 of a centavo softer at 7.8900/7.9000.
The same-day peso had closed earlier 2.05 centavos weaker at 7.9250/7.9330 per dollar.
The main budget provision that interested traders was the government's average exchange rate forecast of 8.53 pesos per dollar for 1997.

Traders said the 48-hour peso closed firmer than the 24-hour contract because dollars bought at 48 hours do not have to be paid for until after the U.S. Veterans' Day holiday on Monday, and may meanwhile be invested in the Mexican money market.
Despite the late flow of dollars into the foreign exchange market, traders said they expected the peso to slide toward the 8 per dollar level during the coming sessions.
Traders said they expected the peso to be unsteady in the short run due to local elections on Sunday, and the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on November 13.
Dealers also expected the peso to soften on Friday due to dealers wanting to close dollar positions prior to the weekend.
